about: Every proposal version Claude made (paid output, never rebuilt) and every rule id ever handed out.

heard-20261008-3614.name: ago = qabel + number + noun
heard-20261008-3614.one_line: To say 'ago', put قبل in front of the number and time unit: قبل ثلاث سنين means three years ago.
heard-20261008-3614.formula: qabel + number + plural time unit (qabel talat sneen)

examples.arabic: قبل كم يوم من السفرة بتحجز التذكرة؟
examples.english: How many days before the trip do you book the ticket?

heard-20261008-3614.why: English puts 'ago' after the time phrase, but Arabic puts قبل in front of the number.

overlaps.name: number + noun
overlaps.why: Both use a number with a plural noun after it; this rule adds قبل in front of the whole phrase.

checked.why: No existing rule or proposal teaches 'ago' with قبل before a number and time unit; E1/E3 cover number+noun forms and the others are different uses of قبل.

heard-20261008-3746.name: hidden gender: nature words
heard-20261008-3746.one_line: Some nature nouns look or sound masculine but are feminine (sun, fire, earth, sky), while هواء (air) is masculine even though it sounds feminine.
heard-20261008-3746.formula: shams / nar / ard / sama = feminine; hawa = masculine

examples.english: So when does the sun rise?

heard-20261008-3746.why: The gender of these nature nouns does not match their sound, so a learner cannot guess it from the word's shape.

overlaps.name: gender on adjectives
overlaps.why: A8 says a feminine noun takes a feminine adjective, but it assumes you already know which nouns are feminine; this rule supplies that for nature words.

checked.why: No existing rule or proposal covers hidden grammatical gender of nature nouns like sun, fire, sky; A8 and A10 only cover agreement, not which nouns are feminine.

heard-20261010-2900.name: kamaan at the end = also
heard-20261010-2900.one_line: To say 'also / too', put kamaan at the very end of the sentence, after the thing it adds to.

examples.english: This is my fiancée's favorite dish too.

examples.arabic: هذي الأكلة المفضلة عند خطيبتي كمان.
examples.english: This dish is my fiancée's favorite too.

heard-20261010-2900.why: English puts 'also' near the verb; she moved kamaan to the end of the sentence for 'too'.

checked.why: No existing rule or proposal says kamaan goes at the end of the sentence to mean 'also'; P-FA-d28341e4 covers a different kamaan ('another', before the noun).

drf1l2k5c.name: awal / aa5er with el-
drf1l2k5c.one_line: Awal and aa5er + a noun without el- mean first / last, but with el- or a possessive ending they mean the beginning / end of, so for 'my first day' use illi or put the adjective after the noun.
drf1l2k5c.formula: awal / aa5er + noun = first / last; awal / aa5er + el- or ending + noun = beginning / end of
drf1l2k5c.why: English uses 'first' and 'last' the same way everywhere, but in Arabic el- or a possessive ending on the noun turns them into 'the beginning of' and 'the end of', because idafa overrules the other rules.

overlaps.name: awal / oola: before or after the noun
overlaps.why: A13 already covers awal + noun versus awal + el- + noun, and a learner could mix it up with this rule.

nlz18hhxs.name: taani and 8eir
nlz18hhxs.one_line: taani before a noun means second; after the noun without el- it means another; 8eir before a noun means a different or other one, and 8eir + 3an means different from.
nlz18hhxs.formula: taani + noun = second | el- + noun + el-taani = the second / the other | noun + taani = another | 8eir + noun = different / other
nlz18hhxs.why: English uses different words for second, another and different, but Arabic uses the same words, so the meaning depends on word order and context.

overlaps.name: taani: before or after the noun
overlaps.why: A14 also covers taani before or after the noun, with and without el-.

1txa2kjvs.name: a8lab and nafs + definite noun
1txa2kjvs.one_line: a8lab (most of) and nafs (the same) are followed by a definite noun, meaning el- + noun or a noun with a possessive ending.
1txa2kjvs.formula: a8lab / nafs + el- + noun (or noun + possessive ending)
1txa2kjvs.why: English says 'most people' and 'the same road' with no marker on the noun, but here the noun after a8lab or nafs must be definite, and a noun with a possessive ending already counts as definite.

overlaps.name: nafs + el-: the same
overlaps.why: A17 also covers nafs + el- + noun = the same, so a learner could mix up the two cards, while a8lab follows the same pattern with a different meaning.

c404ipjzg.name: mufaddal + 3ind
c404ipjzg.one_line: Mufaddal (favorite) is an adjective that follows its noun and matches it in gender and definiteness; a noun with a pronoun ending counts as definite, so it takes el-mufaddal, and 3ind + the person can support it when it stands alone or after the noun.

examples.english: this is his favorite ice cream

c404ipjzg.why: English puts 'favorite' before the noun and never changes it, but in Arabic mufaddal comes after the noun and has to agree with it, and 3ind makes it a matter of preference.

overlaps.name: noun + adjective
overlaps.why: Mufaddal is an adjective that goes after its noun, and el- placement and gender follow the same noun + adjective pattern.

92zgc00ct.why: This is an instruction to update an existing collocations rule with a list from another document, not a new grammar rule, and it has no rule content or examples to turn into a card.
